insights.summary: Q1 FY27 revenue grew 32% to ₹412.5 Cr and gross margin jumped to 24.65%, giving EBITDA of ₹52.8 Cr (12.8%) and PAT of ₹28.9 Cr (7.0%). Management raised FY27 guidance to 30% revenue growth and a 75-100 bps rise in PAT margin, crediting higher realisations (laptop ASP up 12% YoY), wider distribution and gains on inventory bought before component prices rose. Volumes grew 18%; inventory was about ₹700 Cr and net debt about ₹406 Cr.

what_changed.text: Revenue growth guidance raised to 30% from 25%
PAT margin expansion raised to 75-100 bps from 50 bps
Redington added to Ingram and Supertron as national distributors

tone.label: confident
tone.quote: We have started the year comfortably ahead of our FY27 guidance

analyst_questions.answer: International gross margin near 30% vs 21% in India; more sales in the US and Europe (47% of revenue).
Yes, buying ahead of price rises is lifting gross margin; inventory ~₹700 Cr.
Used-laptop buying prices trail new-laptop prices; contracts let it buy at old prices for now.
Q1 is a seasonally weak quarter; management does not expect growth to slow.

red_flags.text: Net debt rose about ₹100 Cr in the quarter to ~₹406 Cr.
Part of the margin gain is from inventory bought before prices rose, which may not last.
Other expenses up 68% YoY on sales incentives.
Volume growth (18%) much lower than revenue growth (32%).

watch_next: Employee and other costs vs revenue

business_snapshot.what_they_make: Premium refurbished laptops and desktops with 1-3 year warranties (Electronics Bazaar)
business_snapshot.customers: Businesses and education buyers through dealers and distributors (Redington, Ingram, Supertron) in 49 countries
business_snapshot.revenue_mix: Q1 FY27: India 36%, Middle East 12%, US 24%, Europe 23%, others 5%; 108,000 laptops and 42,000 others
business_snapshot.demand_drivers: New-PC price inflation from the memory shortage, students and SMEs needing affordable computers, trust in warranties
